sentences.text: 1. Considered IA No.6590/2024, which is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay in filing the appeal.
2. In the application it has been stated that the appellant was not aware of the fact that the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal can be enhanced hence did not prefer any appeal at that time.

However subsequently on contacting another counsel he was made aware that there is possibility of enhancement of the amount of compensation hence the appeal has thereafter been preferred.
Though in the reply respondent No.3 has stated that no particulars or sufficient reasons have been given by the appellant for condonation of delay in filing the appeal but in my opinion the cause shown by the appellant appears to be genuine and reasonable.
IA No.6590/2024 is accordingly allowed and the delay in filing the appeal is condoned.

3. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9366 2 MA-4331-2024 heard.

4. This appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 21.12.2021 passed in MACC No.1617/2018 Pushpendrasingh vs Komal S/O Shri Amarlal Yadav Dwara ... on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45777958/
1 by the 2nd Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Indore whereby a total sum of Rs.40,274/-
has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
5. As per the appellant, on 23.10.2017, at about 11.00 p.m., he along with his father Bhagwansingh was going on a motor cycle.

At that time respondent No.1 drove vehicle a Truck bearing registration No.MP-09-HF-1276 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against his motor cycle as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
He was taken to the hospital for treatment where he remained under treatment for a considerable period of time.
6. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the Claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.20,00,000/- to him by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement to the same.
After evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

7. This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that the amounts which have been awarded to him by the Tribunal under various heads are grossly inadequate.
In the accident the appellant had suffered grievous injuries.
His father had also expired.
He underwent treatment for a period of eight days in two different hospitals.
Due to the injuries suffered by him he experienced a great deal of pain.
He also had to suffer mental agony.

For all this period he required an attendant and also had to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9366 3 MA-4331-2024 take special diet.
It is hence submitted that the amount of compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal be enhanced appropriately.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
9. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
10. As a result of the accident the appellant remained under treatment for a period of eight days and had to be shifted from one hospital to the other.
He had received grievous injuries on his head the effects of which he is still suffering.
Injuries were also received by him on various parts of his body.
His father had also expired as a result of the accident.
The Claims Tribunal has however awarded compensation to the appellant under the general head of attendant, special diet and transportation which in my opinion ought to have been awarded individually.
No amount has been awarded for the injury suffered by the appellant and the amount awarded towards medical expenses is also inadequate.

Considering the nature of the injuries received by the appellant he deserves to be awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/- for the same, a sum of Rs.18,000/- for medical expenses,
Rs.12,000/- for loss of income, Rs.15,000/- for pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.10,000/- each for attendant, special diet and transportation.
Pushpendrasingh vs Komal S/O Shri Amarlal Yadav Dwara ... on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45777958/
2 11.
The appellant is hence entitled for award of a total sum of Rs.85,000/- to him whereas the Claims Tribunal has erred in awarding him a sum of Rs.40,274/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation by Rs.44,376/- which shall be payable to him along with the same rate of interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the date of filing NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9366 4 MA-4331-2024 of the claim application till date of payment.
12. The appeal is accordingly allowed and disposed off.
